items.reason: Detail `s` uses the same status-menu constructor and container actions as the row list.
Detail `y` opens the container’s Copy menu without immediately copying.
Detail `m` opens the Mute menu targeting the detail’s container.
Both levels dispatch `I` through the shared runShortcutVerb helper.
View returns viewDetail before modal rendering, so the drain picker remains invisible while capturing input.
The peek’s direct `y` and `p` dispatch branches are removed.
Neither detail list retains a direct `p` handler.
Existing item and artifact `r` menu handlers remain available in lists and peeks.
Status refusal uses the shared wording and writes to the detail’s rendered flash.
Copy refusal uses the shared wording and writes to the detail’s rendered flash.
Mute refusal uses the shared wording and writes to the detail’s rendered flash.
Container menus occupy the detail Frame’s reserved Block and reduce its list budget.
Detail menus delegate navigation and entry dispatch to the existing row-list menu handlers.
Menu Escape clears the menu without clearing the detail.
Detail openers bypass Selection handling and construct singular container menus.
`/` starts detail search; Enter commits it and restores ordinary detail key handling.
Shared filtering ANDs case-insensitive substring terms across item ID, title and type.
Item search fields exclude status.
Artifact filtering uses the same grammar over name and type.
Escape restores the previously applied term and its filtered lists.
Search opens with an empty buffer, and committing it restores all rows.
Typing forwards ordinary keys, including `j`, `k`, `v` and `r`, to the text field.
Detail synchronization reapplies the active query after polling.
The applied term appears in the non-BROKEN detail header.
Empty search results name the query and explain `/` then Enter to clear.
Artifact availability comes from the unfiltered collection, preserving `v` after filtering empties a list.
Detail search state is separate from row-list search state and disappears when the detail closes.
Detail hints name `r`, `s`, `y`, `m` and `/` without flat copy shortcuts.
Peek hints remove direct copy-name and copy-path keys.
The typing hint names only apply, cancel and help.
Detail help includes menus, applicable `I`, search and conditional clearing; peek help removes flat copies.
Help selects container-menu entries over a detail and has a dedicated detail-search typing branch.

scores.rationale: Shared helpers and focused tests support maintainability, but the invisible drain picker is a significant correctness gap missing from the new tests.

scores.rationale: Shared routing and filtering are maintainable and broadly tested, but the invisible drain picker is a significant integration gap missing from coverage.

accepted.behaviour: When `I` inside the detail view of a Task set with no Worktree binding opens the drain picker, the picker shows on screen over the detail.
accepted.reason: The spec (spec.md:10-11, 21, 70) says that `I` in a detail view runs the container's own verb, so the keyboard in the detail is the same as on the row list. In the Reference, `View` returns the detail before it checks `drainPick`. The picker receives keys, but you cannot see it. The spec wins; this is a defect in the Reference.
